metadata.title: MAPP 6020.2 Rev.1 Applications for Parenteral Products in Plastic Immediate Containers
metadata.legal_basis: CDER Manual of Policies and Procedures (internal FDA review procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.
metadata.applicability: FDA staff procedure. Category: New Drug Review.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement:  An application for approval of a parenteral product in a plastic immediate container for which the container requires animal studies beyond limited confirmatory testing and the testing described in the USP to show that the drug product is safe must be submitted as an NDA under section 505(b).
candidates.context:  An application for approval of a parenteral product in a plastic immediate container may be filed as an ANDA under section 505(j) provided that: (1) the product duplicates an approved product listed in the current edition of Approved Drug Products With Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (also known as The Orange Book); and (2) approval of the product in the plastic immediate container does not require studies beyond limited confirmatory testing and the testing described in the United States Pharmacopoeia (USP) (e.g., <661> and <381>).  An application for approval of a parenteral product in a plastic immediate container containing an active ingredient or a combination of active ingredients not previously approved under an application submitted under section 505(b), including an application for a product currently marketed in a glass container for which there is no reference listed dru

candidates.statement:  An application for approval of a parenteral product in a plastic immediate container containing an active ingredient or a combination of active ingredients not previously approved under an application submitted under section 505(b), including an application for a product currently marketed in a glass container for which there is no reference listed drug, should be filed as an NDA under section 505(b).
candidates.context:  An application for approval of a parenteral product in a plastic immediate container for which the container requires animal studies beyond limited confirmatory testing and the testing described in the USP to show that the drug product is safe must be submitted as an NDA under section 505(b).  Applications filed for approval of new drugs under section 505(b) are required to contain evidence of safety and effectiveness. Published reports may be adequate for certain applications. However, reference to general recognition of safety and effectiveness is an inadequate basis for approval of a new drug.

candidates.statement:  Applications filed for approval of new drugs under section 505(b) are required to contain evidence of safety and effectiveness. Published reports may be adequate for certain applications. However, reference to general recognition of safety and effectiveness is an inadequate basis for approval of a new drug.
candidates.context:  An application for approval of a parenteral product in a plastic immediate container containing an active ingredient or a combination of active ingredients not previously approved under an application submitted under section 505(b), including an application for a product currently marketed in a glass container for which there is no reference listed drug, should be filed as an NDA under section 505(b).  Applications filed under section 505(b) for parenteral products in plastic containers that meet the definition of a human drug application in section 735 of the FD&C Act are subject to user fees.
